discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 221627
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
1127 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Very mild once again before a cold front arrives to northwest
  Indiana late this afternoon.

- There is a 60% to 80% chance of showers starting early this
  afternoon. Rain amounts will be 0.10" or less. Rain exits by
  late evening. 

- Seasonably cold this week with highs near 40.

- Periods of rain and snow showers Wednesday evening through 
  Thursday (40-50% chance).

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 211 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

High temperatures Saturday afternoon were a single degree shy of a 
1913 record at both Fort Wayne and South Bend amid an unseasonable 
500-mb ridge over the eastern CONUS. We'll cling to one more mild 
November day as the upper-air pattern remains amplified ahead of an 
approaching cold front. Filtered sunshine to begin the day followed 
by increasing clouds and rain arriving from east to east by the 
early afternoon. Somewhat breezy as well with southwest winds of 20-
25 mph. Rain amounts remain modest at 0.10" or less owing to the 
late-day timing and upper-level forcing displaced well to the 
northwest. Cool northwest flow sets in by the early evening hours 
propelling Sunday night lows toward freezing (clouds may keep 
northwest OH in the upper-30s). 

Very brief and inconsequential lake response from a secondary surge 
of cold air advection Monday night. Fetch and incoming high pressure 
limit the overall moister depth, but increasing concensus yields 
a narrow area (in both time and space) for 20% POPs. 

For late-week, the ECMWF has joined the GFS in what strikes me as an 
unusual evolution of dual upper-level lows emerging over the central 
and southern US. Concensus revels a deep trough in the lee of the 
Rockies, extending through far southern Texas. Encountering a 
subtropical ridge off the Florida coast this energy is shunted 
poleward along and east of the Mississippi River. The result is 
strong moisture transport and lackluster cold air given the 
competing air masses. POPs have increased locally to a 40-50% chance 
Wednesday evening through Tuesday with precipitation types generally 
following a diurnal curve (rain/snow overnight, changing to rain 
during the day).  The primary trough responsible for this system 
arrives to the west Coast tonight, improving model-guidance sampling 
in the near future.

In the wake of this feature, troughing favors the Midwest through 
the Thanksgiving weekend while zonal flow resumes for the start of 
December.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z MONDAY/...
Issued at 1127 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

A relatively strong cold front swings east through KSBN around
21z, and 23/00z at KFWA. Narrow moisture plume accompanying the
frontal interface and incoming shortwave energy should result in
a ~4 hour period or so of light rain, along with ceilings 
lowering into low MVFR. A period of IFR also possible immediately
along the front, best chances at KSBN where a tempo IFR group  
was retained. Breezy northwest winds post-frontal otherwise 
into tonight with MVFR stratocu expected to scatter out to 
primarily VFR. 

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 3 PM this afternoon to 4 AM EST 
     Tuesday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Brown
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.text:
SPC AC 221632

   Day 1 Convective Outlook CORR 1
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1032 AM CST Sun Nov 22 2026

   Valid 221630Z - 231200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON
   AND EVENING OVER PARTS OF SOUTH TEXAS....

   CORRECTED FOR UPDATED THUNDER FORECAST

   ...SUMMARY...
   Strong to locally severe storms are possible across parts of South
   Texas, mainly during the afternoon and early evening.

   ...South TX...
   A large upper trough is moving eastward across the Plains states
   today, with an expansive surface cold front sagging across TX and
   the lower MS Valley.  Ahead of the front, dewpoints in the 60s and
   strong daytime heating will yield an axis of CAPE from south TX into
   parts of LA/AR.  The greatest instability will reside over south TX,
   where ~2000 J/kg of MLCAPE will promote the development of a few
   afternoon thunderstorms capable of hail and gusty winds.  The
   activity will move offshore after dark, ending the threat.  

   ...Southern AR...
   Farther north, another cluster of thunderstorms may pose a localized
   risk of hail or gusty winds over southern AR/northern LA.  However
   very minimal instability suggests the severe threat here is below
   MRGL thresholds.

   ..Hart/Barnes.. 11/22/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 221709

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1109 AM CST Sun Nov 22 2026

   Valid 231200Z - 241200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely Monday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper-level trough will move through the Great Lakes into the
   Northeast on Monday. Short-wave ridging will develop over the
   Mid-South and Southeast. Another weaker upper trough will approach
   the Trans-Pecos by early Tuesday morning. At the surface, high
   pressure will become more expansive across much of the CONUS.
   Offshore flow will be present from the Gulf into the East Coast.

   Early period thunderstorms are possible near the front in the Lower
   Mississippi Valley and South Texas. Limited buoyancy--decreasing
   with time--will preclude severe weather with this activity.
   Isolated, elevated thunderstorms may also occur with the trough
   within Trans-Pecos/Permian Basin late Monday night/early Tuesday
   morning. Severe weather is not likely with these storms as well.

   ..Wendt.. 11/22/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 220830

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0230 AM CST Sun Nov 22 2026

   Valid 241200Z - 251200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated thunderstorms are possible over parts of the Gulf Coast and
   West Coast Tuesday. Severe storms are not expected.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough over the southern Plains is forecast to intensify as
   it moves southeastward across TX toward the Gulf Coast Tuesday and
   Tuesday night. In the wake of a prior cold front, low-level moisture
   will remain confined near the Gulf Coast across TX and into the
   Southeast. Scattered thunderstorms are expected along typical sea
   breeze corridors across the FL Peninsula during the day. Strong
   mid-level ascent from the approaching trough and a weak surface
   low/inverted surface trough over the Gulf may also support an
   elevated band of showers and isolated thunderstorms over parts of
   MS/AL Tuesday night into early Wednesday.

   To the west, an approaching Pacific trough and cold front are
   forecast to move inland across northern CA into early Wednesday.
   Onshore flow may support weak buoyancy along the coast, with a
   narrow band of shallow convection potentially supporting occasional
   lightning flashes into Wednesday morning. Given the weak overall
   buoyancy and poor overlap with strong vertical shear, severe storms
   are not expected.

   ..Lyons.. 11/22/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
